title: Retention
subtitle: Segment files, cleanup policies (delete vs compact), and tiered cloud object storage.
keyTakeaways: Kafka partitions are physically split into immutable segment files (typically 1 GB each) to enable O(1) garbage collection.
The `delete` cleanup policy purges whole segment files based on time or size; the `compact` policy retains the latest state per key.
Tiered Storage (KIP-405) offloads sealed historical segments to cheap cloud object storage (S3/GCS), enabling years of retention at low cost.

sections.heading: Segment Files and Cleanup Policies: Delete vs Compact
sections.body: A Kafka partition is not a single giant file on disk. Appending millions of records to a single multi-terabyte file would make deleting expired records an expensive O(N) file rewriting operation. Instead, Kafka divides each partition into immutable segment files (default: 1 GB or 7 days). Only the most recent segment (the Active Segment) is open for writes.
bullets: Delete Policy (`cleanup.policy = delete`): Segments whose newest record is older than `retention.ms` (e.g., 7 days) are deleted wholesale from the filesystem in an instantaneous O(1) OS operation.

Compact Policy (`cleanup.policy = compact`): Preserves the latest value for each message key across the topic. Background cleaner threads scan closed segments and purge older duplicate keys, creating an append-only changelog of entity state (used by Kafka Streams KTable and database CDC topics).

Tombstones: To delete a key under log compaction, produce a message with that key and a `null` payload. Compaction retains the tombstone for a delete retention window before permanently erasing the key.

codeSnippet.title: Compacted CDC Topic Configuration for Database State Snapshots
codeSnippet.code:
kafka-topics --bootstrap-server broker:9092 --create \
  --topic customer-account-state \
  --partitions 8 \
  --replication-factor 3 \
  --config cleanup.policy=compact \
  --config min.cleanable.dirty.ratio=0.5 \
  --config delete.retention.ms=86400000 # 24hr tombstone retention

sections.heading: Tiered Storage (KIP-405)
sections.body: Historically, retaining months of Kafka data required attaching tens of terabytes of expensive NVMe SSD storage directly to broker instances. Tiered Storage decouples storage capacity from broker compute.
bullets: Local Tier: Fast NVMe storage retains only the active segment and recent segments (e.g., 2 to 24 hours), serving 99% of real-time consumer traffic from RAM and local disk.

Remote Tier: Once a segment is sealed, Kafka asynchronously copies it to cloud object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob). Consumers replaying historical data stream segments directly from S3 without consuming broker local disk space.

tradeOffs.pros: Maintains complete current state snapshot for every key; allows fast consumer state restoration from scratch.
tradeOffs.cons: Background cleaning consumes broker CPU and disk IOPS; requires careful tombstone management.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Database CDC event streams, configuration catalogs, and Kafka Streams state stores.

tradeOffs.pros: Deterministic storage footprint; simple O(1) segment deletions with zero CPU cleaning overhead.
tradeOffs.cons: Older events vanish regardless of whether they represent the latest state of an entity.
tradeOffs.bestFor: High-volume telemetry metrics, clickstream logs, and ephemeral notification events.

interviewTip: Explain Log Compaction in event-sourcing and CDC architectures: 'For database changelog topics, we configure `cleanup.policy=compact`. Kafka retains the latest update for every primary key indefinitely, allowing new microservices to reconstruct a full database replica from scratch simply by consuming the topic from offset zero.'
